Brake discs, transport protection covers

Remove the transport protection covers from the brake discs. Separate the cover by using a pair of pliers to pull the wire through a hole in the wheel from the outside. Then remove the cover from the inside of the wheel without removing the wheel.
Certificate of Conformity

🔧 Online öffnen

Certificate of Conformity
Cars for EU market:
The “Certificate of Conformity” is in the glove box. This document is to be folded and placed together with the other vehicle documents.
⚠️ Note
| The document is an item of value that must be carried in the car.
Paint protector

🔧 Online öffnen

Paint protector
General
The paint protector may be left on the car for a maximum of three months before removal.


The date of manufacture of the car is given on the vehicle card (422 means week 42 day 2).


[/images/9-3-9440/img-d8/d890m005.svg](saabwisonline.com/images/9-3-9440/img-d8/d890m005.svg)

Location
/images/9-3-9440/img-f8/f845m002.svg
Paint protector is fitted in the following locations:
| • | the sills (Aero) | | • | the boot lid/tailgate | | • | the bonnet | | • | the roof | | • | the driver’s side rear door | Removing
The paint protector may be removed with temperatures in the range 0 to +35°C; the most suitable temperature is +20°C. If the body and the ambient temperatures are above +35°C, park the car in the shade or cool it down with water until the body has attained a suitable temperature.
⚠️ Important
| Adhesive residue may fasten to the paintwork at high temperatures.
|
The paint protector must be removed at least 48 hours before the car is shown to a customer so that any swelling has time to go down.


Loosen the corners of the paint protector. Use your hands only; no tools


Hold the paint protector as close as possible to the bodywork.


Pull parallel to the body surface at an even rate, do not jerk .


Wash the car with water and dry it


Make sure there is no adhesive residue remaining. If there is, remove it with petroleum spirit (low-aromatic petroleum hydrocarbon) or Isopropanol (Isopropyl alcohol). Use these sparingly and for short periods only.
When the paint protector and any adhesive residue has been removed, there may be swelling in paintwork. This is normally temporary and will disappear within 48 hours.


Road test

🔧 Online öffnen

Road test
Function checks
The road test is an important part of the service programme. Check the functionality of the various components and systems as described below.

| • | Lighting: Check front and rear lights, direction indicators, brake lights, high-level brake light, rear fog lights and number plate illumination. | | • | Ignition switch: Check that the gear-lever lock operates satisfactorily and that the key is easy to insert and remove. Check the parking position lock on cars with automatic transmission (certain markets only). | | • | Engine: Check function and noise level. Make sure the engine acceleration is normal. | | • | Clutch: Check the clutch disengagement and engagement positions. | | • | Manual gearbox: Check gearbox operation and noise level. | | • | Automatic transmission: Check the starting interlock, i.e. that the engine can be started only when the selector lever is in P or N, noise levels and shifting performance. | | • | Wheels: Check wheel balance and wheel roundness. | | • | Steering: Check the straight-ahead position of the steering wheel, directional stability and operation of the power steering system. | | • | Instruments and indicator lamps: Check the operation of instruments and indicator lamps. | | • | Brakes: Check brake pedal travel, handbrake lever travel (1-4 notches) and the efficiency of the brakes and handbrake. | | • | Cruise Control: Check the functionality of the Cruise Control system. | | • | Heating and ventilation unit: Check the operation of the A/C system and controls. When the outdoor temperature is so low that the A/C cannot be turned on, check its operation indoors. | | • | Wipers and washers: Check the washer jet pattern and wiper operation on the windscreen. | | • | Check that the clock shows the right time. |  Bear in mind the customer’s expectations!
 Wipe the steering wheel and gear lever clean and make sure that all other traces of pre-delivery inspection and service work have been removed.


 Return the driver's seat to its original position if it has been readjusted.

Removable towbar
Clean the ball unit and its mounting as necessary. Check that the ball unit is easy to remove/fit and that it locks properly. For lubrication, use a base oil with anti-corrosion properties and a broad temperature range.
Lubricating the detachable towbar from Bosal


Clean and lubricate the coupling mechanism. Lubricate the pin on the top of the towbar as well as the lock cylinder.


Clean and lubricate the towbar bracket.


Configuration of dipped beam/front fog lights

🔧 Online öffnen

Configuration of dipped beam/front fog lights
Adjust
As part of the pre-delivery service, make the following settings on cars for the SE market. These settings prevent dipped beam and the front fog lights from being on at the same time.



Connect Tech 2 and select F0: Diagnose


Select the model year and car model.


Select F4: All


Select ” Most Common Adjustments”


Select ” Fog Lights Front”


Press the ” Select” button


Select ” Pos 1 (and 2 if High Beam) (Special)”


For programming, select OK ⚠️ Note If the car is not configured for fog lights but fog lights are installed, the message “Fog lights not installed!” will appear in Tech2.


Advanced voice recognition

🔧 Online öffnen

Advanced voice recognition
Only one language is activated in cars with the navigation system and advanced voice recognition. Accordingly, the appropriate language for the market must be activated prior to delivery as described below.


From Tech 2 select: Service Programming System (SPS)


Request control module data: Model year → 2005 Model → Saab 9-3 Sport (9440) System → Body Body → ICM3 (OCP)


Finish reading out the control module data and connect Tech 2 to a computer with TIS2000.


Start TIS2000. Select Service Programming System


Select Tech 2 and continue. Confirm the VIN. Make sure that the correct control module has been selected.


Select Language. Select the desired language from the menu. If ”M3318: ECU already contains the latest program version. Reprogramming not possible.” appears, the ICM3 already contains the correct language. Finish.


If this message does not appear, continue by selecting ”Next →”.


Download the new language to Tech 2.


Disconnect Tech 2 from the computer and connect it to the car.


Remove the navigation disc from the DVD player in the car and insert the CD with TIS2000 ICM3 Edition 2004-1 or later version of TIS2000 ICM3.


From Tech 2 select: Service Programming System (SPS). Select Program ECU. Wait until the update is finished. Progress is not shown on Tech 2 but on the ICM3 display.

Basic Engine — Adjustment/replacement Procedures
Power train removal

🔧 Online öffnen

Power train removal
To remove
| Warning
There is a large number of cables, hoses, wires, etc., that are secured with hard plastic cable ties. After tightening, the loose ends of these cable ties are cut off and may leave more or less sharp edges at fixing points.
Pay attention to the risk of cuts caused by these sharp ends! | 1. Place the car on a lift and apply wing covers.


Open the cap on the expansion tank.


Raise the car slightly and remove the front wheels.


Remove the lower spoiler shield. Unplug and remove the connector.


Place a receptacle under the car, connect a hose to the radiator and drain the coolant.


Remove the wing liners from both front wheel housings and the cover by the gearbox.


Detach the hose for the headlamp washers and drain the washer fluid reservoir.


Lower the car slightly and remove the bumper.


Remove the cover on the left-hand side and the charge air hose between the charge air pipe and the charge air cooler.


Remove the lower charge air pipe bracket from the fan cowling.


Remove the cover on the right-hand side and the hose between the charge air cooler and the charge air pipe.


Remove the dryer filter bolts from the radiator.


Remove the lower seal between the charge air cooler and the radiator.


Lower the car and remove the upper engine cover.


Remove the battery cover and the battery cooler pipe.


Undo the bonnet cable quick-release coupling by first undoing the clip in the body and then separating the quick-release coupling. Use a screwdriver.


Remove the upper radiator member.


Unplug the connector to the pressure/temperature sensor and disconnect the bypass valve hose.


Detach the charge air hose from the throttle body and undo the upper charge air pipe bracket from the fan cowling. Remove the pipe with hose.


Remove the battery.


Detach the ventilation hose from the radiator.


Detach the vacuum hose quick-release coupling form the vacuum pump.


Aut: Unplug the connector to the TCM. Remove the cover with the control module. Unplug the connector under the control module.


Undo the main fuse box in front of the battery tray and move it aside.


Unplug the bonnet switch connector, undo the cable clip and remove the battery tray.


Unplug the connector and undo the clips securing the cables on the fan cowling.


Unplug the reversing light switch connector.


Remove the seal over the radiator core.


Remove the upper radiator brackets from the body.


Unplug both connectors from the left-hand structural member. Auto: Detach the oil pipes from the fluid cooler. Use 87 92 806 Removal tool, automatic transmission oil pipes .


Remove the fan cowling retaining bolts and loosen the cowling slightly.


Secure the condenser and the charge air cooler to the body with cable ties.


Remove the fan cowling. Carefully detach the A/C pipes from their retaining clips on the right structural member.


Place a receptacle under the radiator and remove the lower radiator hose.


Remove the upper radiator hose.


Remove the radiator.


Unplug the connector for the A/C pressure sensor.


Detach the hoses from the turbo inlet pipe and remove the turbo inlet pipe. Unplug the mass air flow sensor connector. Plug the turbo inlet.


Remove the air cleaner cover and the air cleaner. Detach the inlet hose and remove the air cleaner casing.


Remove the windscreen washer filler pipe.


Remove the cover on the main fuse box and undo the two retaining screws.


Disconnect the positive cable from the battery.


Undo the retaining screw on the engine harness connector in the main fuse box.


Remove the engine harness clamp from the body and the ground cables.


Bend up the engine harness and secure it to the engine with e.g. 83 95 212 Strap .


Unplug the coolant level connector. Detach the expansion tank from the body and secure it to the engine. Use 83 95 212 Strap .


Undo the coolant hose quick-release couplings while trapping any coolant spill, bend aside and secure the hoses to the engine.


Detach the gear cables from the gearbox, carefully bend them aside and secure them to the expansion tank bracket on the body with cable ties.


Fit 30 07 739 Hose pinch-off pliers to the clutch hose and disconnect the quick-release coupling from the clutch slave cylinder. ⚠️ Warning The work involved in removing the fuel pipe requires working with the vehicle’s fuel system. The following points should therefore be heeded in conjunction with these measures: • Have a class BE fire extinguisher on hand! Be aware of the risk of sparks, i.e. in connection with electric circuits, short-circuiting, etc. • Absolutely No Smoking! • Ensure good ventilation! If there is approved ventilation for evacuating fuel fumes then this must be used. • Wear protective gloves! Prolonged exposure of the hands to fuel can cause irritation to the skin. • Wear protective goggles.


Release any pressure in the fuel system by carefully pressing the service valve needle. Collect any fuel spill. Detach both fuel lines from the fuel rail while gripping the lower nut. Plug the fuel lines. Use 82 92 948 Plugs, A/C system assy .


Disconnect the quick-release coupling for the ventilation line and detach the fuel lines and ventilation lines from the clips on the camshaft cover. Bend up the ventilation hose from the intake manifold and place it on the camshaft cover.


Check and adjust the steering wheel and the steering assembly so that they are pointing straight ahead. ⚠️ Warning In order to avoid the contact roller for the airbag twisting and breaking the steering wheel must be secured via the steering column lock or by taping it to the panel.


Detach the steering shaft from the steering gear.

Symptom: Oil discoloured reddish.
Fault symptom
Oil discoloured reddish.

Criteria
When checking the oil level, the oil appears discoloured. This is due to an oil leak detection agent used in production on a certain percentage of engines.

Procedure
No measures required. Neither the oil nor the engine are faulty as a result.

Fit a new sealing ring. Check that this is seated properly.


Plug in the connectors to the fuel level sensor and fuel pump.


Carefully thread the cover into the maintenance hole.


Fit the circlip. Turn clockwise.


Remove the plugs and fit the fuel line.


Fit the connector.


Fit the fuel tank. Refer to Fuel tank, EU .


Fuel pump

🔧 Online öffnen

Fuel pump
| Warning
The work involved in removing the fuel pump requires working with the vehicle’s fuel system. The following points should therefore be heeded in conjunction with these measures:
•
Have a class BE fire extinguisher on hand! Be aware of the risk of sparks, i.e. in connection with electric circuits, short-circuiting, etc.
•
Absolutely No Smoking!
•
Ensure good ventilation! If there is approved ventilation for evacuating fuel fumes then this must be used.
•
Wear protective gloves! Prolonged exposure of the hands to fuel can cause irritation to the skin.
•
Wear protective goggles. | ⚠️ Important
| Be particulary observant regardning cleanliness when working on the fuel system. Loss of function may occur due to very small particles. Prevent dirt and grime from entering the fuel system by cleaning the connections and plugging pipes and lines during disassembly. Use 82 92 948 Plugs, A/C system assembly. Keep components free from contaminants during storage.
|
To remove


Remove the fuel tank. Refer to Fuel tank, To remove .


To prevent dirt entering the fuel system, clean the outside of the tank if necessary before removing the fuel pump.


Unplug the fuel pump connector.


On cars with ORVR, unplug the connector for the pressure sensor.


Remove the fuel pump. Use tool 83 96 194 Fitting tool, fuel armature to undo the fuel pump lock ring.


Disconnect the quick-release couplings on the EVAP emission canister.


Lift up the fuel pump slightly and disconnect the quick-release coupling for the tank ventilation from the fuel pump.


Carefully lift up the fuel pump and place it in a receptacle. ⚠️ Important ⚠️ Take care not to damage the fuel level sensor.


To fit


Fit a new seal.


Lift up the ventilation hose and lower the fuel pump slightly. Secure the ventilation hose to the pump housing and connect it to the pump cover. Lower the fuel pump carefully into the tank.


Make sure the recesses in the tank connection are in line with the corresponding heels on the pump cover.


Make sure the seal is located correctly. Tighten the fuel pump using 83 96 194 Fitting tool, fuel armature .


Connect the quick-release couplings to the EVAP emission canister.


Attach the fuel lines to the fasteners on the fuel tank.


Secure the ventilation line to the outlet in the tank.


Plug in the fuel pump connector.


On cars with ORVR, plug in the connector to the pressure sensor.


Fit the fuel tank. Refer to Fuel tank, To fit .

Undo and remove the cover over the maintenance hole: Carefully raise the threaded cover from over the maintenance hole. Unplug the fuel level sensor.


Remove the sealing ring.


Press out and hold the catches for the fuel level sensor (arrows). Remove the fuel level sensor from the guide.

Plug in the fuel level sensor.


Fit a new sealing ring.


Carefully insert the cover into the maintenance hole.


Fit the circlip. Turn clockwise.


Remove the plugs and fit the fuel line and fuel return line.


Fit the connector.


Fit the fuel tank. Refer to Fuel tank, EU .

Reduce the fuel pressure by removing fuse 2 when the engine is running (fuse 2 is in the electrical box in front of the battery). When the engine has stopped, turn the ignition key to LOCK and refit the fuse.


Raise the car.


Remove the return line from the holder.


Fit the special tool to the fuel filter. Use spacers so that the clamp fits.


Remove the fuel lines from the fuel filter and plug the lines. Only remove the fuel lines once fuel no longer runs out of the fuel filter. Undo the quick couplings with 83 95 261 Tool, fuel line . Plug with 82 92 948 Plugs, AC system, kit.


If the fuel filter is empty: Remove the special tool.


Undo and remove the fuel filter by pressing the fuel filter forward out of the housing. Lift up the catch (arrow).


To fit


Insert a new fuel filter. Slide the filter forward into the housing. Take note of the direction of flow. Make sure the catch engages.


Remove the plugs. Connect the fuel lines with quick couplings to the fuel filter.


Fit the return line into the holder.


Check the seal of the fuel line quick couplings and fuel filter while the engine is running.

Petrol engine: Reduce the fuel pressure by removing fuse 2 while the engine is running (fuse 2 is located in the main fuse box in front of the battery). Once the engine has stopped, turn the ignition key to LOCK and refit the fuse.


Remove the negative cable from the battery.


Z19: Remove the upper engine cover. Remove the panel cover. Press the centre pins out of the clips from the wheel housing side. B207 RHD: Remove the air cleaner assembly.


Unplug the fuel lines in the engine bay, use 83 95 261 Fuel line tool and plug the lines. Use 82 92 948 Plugs, A/C system, kit .


Raise the car.


CV: Fit Chassis reinforcement, front subframe, CV, petrol . or Chassis reinforcement, diesel


Z19: Remove Exhaust pipe, front . B207: Remove the exhaust pipe flange and unload the flexible section using 83 95 212 Strap .


Remove the steering shaft joint from the steering gear.


Remove the rear torque arm bolt.


Unload the subframe using a pillar jack and remove the rear bolts and stays.


Lower the subframe at the rear.


Undo the fuel lines from their holders and the brake pipes from the front holders. ⚠️ Important Be careful that the brake pipes do not get damaged.


Position a receptacle under the car and unplug the fuel lines at the fuel tank and plug them. For diesel and EU tank, use 83 95 261 Fuel line tool .


Lower the pipes.


To fit


Fit the fuel lines in their holders.


Connect the fuel lines to the tank.


Raise the subframe using 83 95 311 Trolley lift with 83 94 801 Parent fixture and 83 96 137 Centring tool, subframe - body . Align the tool to the guide holes in the body. Fit the stays and the bolts. Tightening torque, subframe: 75 Nm + 135° (55 lbf ft +135°) **Tightening torque, stay: 90 Nm + 45° (67 lbf ft + 45°)


Fit the bolt for the torque arm. Tightening torque 80 Nm (59 lbf ft).


Fit the steering shaft joint to the steering gear. Clean the threads and apply Thread locking adhesive, Loctite 242 to the threads. Tightening torque 30 Nm (22 lbf ft) ⚠️ Warning Check that the bolt fits into the groove on the pinion shaft.


Fit the exhaust pipe flange and exhaust pipe mountings. Tightening torque 30 Nm (22 lbf ft) Z19: Fit Exhaust pipe, front .


CV: Fit Chassis reinforcement, front subframe, CV, petrol . or Chassis reinforcement, diesel.


Lower the car.


Connect the fuel lines in the engine bay. (B284 only has delivery line)


B207 RHD: Fit the air cleaner assembly. Z19: Fit the panel cover over the fuel lines and the upper engine cover.


Reconnect the negative battery cable.


Carry out Procedures after reconnecting the battery .


Fuel System — Fault diagnosis Procedures
Damaged fuel filler cap

🔧 Online öffnen

Damaged fuel filler cap
Symptom: Fuel filler cap damaged due to handling error
Fault symptom
Fuel filler cap damaged due to handling error

Criteria
Damage can occur when the fuel filler cap is opened incorrectly.

Procedure
Tell the customer how to open the cap as follows:



Turn the cap anticlockwise 90° while the spring pressure increases.


Turn a further 90° anticlockwise over a click point and against a stop.


Remove the cap.


Close the cap by twisting clockwise until at least three clicks are heard.


Compare List

🔧 Online öffnen


Symptom:

Diagnostic help
To compare the customer's car with another almost identical car, which you know is in full working order, helps to establish whether the customer's problem can be a characteristic of the car's design. To reach a valid conclusion, the comparison should be performed under the same conditions and with the same criteria on a car that has the same optional equipment as the customer's car.

Check valve, crankcase ventilation, checking/replacement


Remove Throttle body actuator unit (604) .


Check the function of the check valve using 30 14 883 Pressure/vacuum pump . Connect the pump with a suitable nozzle to the hole for the check valve.


Is it possible to pump up a pressure? Yes: The check valve is in order. Refit the throttle body. No: The check valve is faulty and must be replaced. Go to step 4.


Remove the intake manifold, intake manifold with SAI.


Press out the check valve.


Fit a new check valve.


Fit the intake manifold, intake manifold with SAI.


Fit Throttle body actuator unit (604) .

Remove Throttle body actuator unit (604)


Remove Control module, Trionic T8 (589)

Remove the atmospheric pressure sensor (539) (B) from the intake manifold. Allow the sensor to hang in the connector.

Fit the intake manifold and position the cable duct without fitting the nuts and screws.


Fit the intake manifold’s stay (B).


Tighten the screws and nuts for the intake manifold (A) Tightening torque, intake manifold, stay 22 Nm (16 lbf ft) **Tightening torque, intake manifold to cylinder head 10 Nm (7 lbf ft)


Fit the dipstick (A).


Guide down the wiring harness’ connector under the intake manifold.


Fit the connector (B) to the clip.


Plug in the injectors’ connector (A) for the engine’s wiring harness.

Fit the brake servo’s plastic hose (B) to the intake manifold.


Fit the EVAP canister purge valve’s hose (A) to the intake manifold.


Fit the fuel pressure regulator’s hose (D) to the intake manifold.


Fit the cable duct’s nut (C).


Fit the atmospheric pressure sensor (B)(539) to the intake manifold.


Fit the solenoid valve’s hose (A) to the intake manifold.

Exhaust pipe, front, B207

🔧 Online öffnen

Exhaust pipe, front, B207
To remove


Raise the car.


Remove the lower engine cover.


Cut the front pipe between the flexipipe and the silencer at 87 mm (see illustration). Cut the pipe at right-angles using 83 95 667 Pipe cutter/exhaust system .


Undo the nuts to the catalytic converter and remove the front pipe.


To fit


Clean the joint on the connecting pipe.


Fit the joint clamp.


Fit the front pipe to the catalytic converter with a new gasket and new nuts. Replace the rubber mountings if necessary. Tightening torque 25 Nm (18.5 lbf ft)


Adjust the joint clamp so that the pipe ends are in the middle of the clamp.


Tighten the joint clamp nuts. Tightening torque 40 Nm (30 lbf ft).


Fit the lower engine cover.


Lower the car.


Connect an exhaust hose and start the engine. Check the exhaust system for leaks.


Silencer, front, B207

🔧 Online öffnen

Silencer, front, B207
To remove


Raise the car.


Cut the front pipe between the flexible section and the silencer to the size given, 87 mm. Use 83 95 667 Pipe cutter/exhaust system .


Cut the exhaust pipe at the rear silencer to the size given, 100 mm. Use 83 95 667 Pipe cutter/exhaust system .


Remove the front silencer.


To fit


Clean the joints and connecting pipe.


Fit the joint clamps.


Fit the front pipe with new rubber mountings.


If necessary also change the rubber mountings for the rear silencer.


Adjust the joint clamps so that the pipe ends are in the middle of the clamp.


Adjust the front and rear silencers so they hang evenly.


For cars with visible tailpipe, adjust this so that it hangs in the centre of the tailpipe cutout in the rear bumper.


Tighten the joint clamp nuts. Tightening torque 40 Nm (30 lbf ft)


Lower the car


Connect an exhaust hose and start the engine. Check the exhaust system for leaks.


Rear silencer

🔧 Online öffnen

Rear silencer
To remove


Raise the car.


Cut the exhaust pipe to dimension, 100 mm. Cut it at right-angles using 83 95 667 Pipe cutter/exhaust system .


Remove the rear silencer.


To fit


Clean the cut to remove burrs and dirt.


Fit the joint clamp on the pipe.


Fit the rear silencer with new rubber mountings.


Change the rubber mountings for the front silencer as well if necessary.


Adjust the joint clamp so that the pipe joint is in the middle of the clamp.


Adjust the front and rear silencers so they balance.


On variants with visible tail pipe: Make sure the tail pipe is positioned centrally in the recess in the rear bumper and follows the profile of the bumper.


Tighten the clamp nuts. Tightening torque 40 Nm (30 lbf ft).


Lower the car.


Connect an exhaust hose and start the engine. Check that the exhaust does not leak.


Exhaust system assembly, B207

🔧 Online öffnen

Exhaust system assembly, B207
To remove


Raise the car.


Cut the front pipe between the flexipipe and the silencer at 87 mm (see illustration). Cut the pipe at right-angles using 83 95 667 Pipe cutter/exhaust system .


Remove the front and rear silencers.


To fit


Clean the joint.


Put on the joint clamp and fit the front silencer with new rubber mountings.


Adjust the joint clamp so that the pipe ends are in the middle of the clamp.


Put on the joint clamp and fit the rear silencer with new rubber mountings.


Adjust the joint clamp so that the pipe ends are in the middle of the clamp.


Adjust the front and rear silencers so they balance. On cars with visible tail pipe, this must be done so that it is positioned centrally in the tail pipe recess in the rear bumper.


Tighten the joint clamps. Tightening torque 40 Nm (30 lbf ft).


Lower the car.


Connect an exhaust hose and start the engine. Check the exhaust system for leaks.


Exhaust manifold

🔧 Online öffnen

Exhaust manifold
To remove


Remove the Turbocharger .


Remove the heat shield.


Remove the exhaust manifold and the stay.


To fit


Clean the contact surfaces from gasket residue and soot.


Fit new gaskets.


Fit the exhaust manifold with new nuts **Tightening torque, Stay I : 25 Nm (18 lbf ft), Stay II : 32 Nm (23 lbf ft)


Fit the exhaust manifold stay. Tightening torque 48 Nm (35 lbf ft)


Fit the heat shield. Tightening torque 22 Nm (16 lbf ft).


Fit the Turbocharger .

Battery check

🔧 Online öffnen

Battery check


Switch off all consumers and remove the key from the ignition switch. ⚠️ Note Certain diagnostic trouble codes can be generated if the battery is tested while the key is in the ignition switch.


Remove the battery cover. ⚠️ Note Low battery electrolyte level is indicated by white showing through the indicator window. A sufficient electrolyte level is indicated by black showing through the indicator window.


Check the electrolyte level. The battery cannot be topped up. If the electrolyte level is too low, the battery must be changed.


Remove the cover from the Underhood Electrical Centre (UEC).


Remove fuses 30 and 37. Wait at least 20 seconds before connecting the battery tester.


Connect the red cable clip to the positive terminal (+). (Reversed polarity will not damage the analyser.)


Connect the black cable clamp to the negative (-) terminal. Make sure the cable clamp makes as good contact as possible. Follow the instructions on the display of the battery analyser. ⚠️ Note Once both clamps are connected, the analyser starts automatically. For a detailed description of how to use the analyser, refer to the analyser’s instruction manual.


Under “SELECT TEST”, select whether the battery is connected to the vehicle electrical system (“IN VEHICLE”) or not (“OUTSIDE OF VEHICLE”). Select (“IN VEHICLE”) as the battery is connected in the vehicle.


Under “BATTERY TYPE”, select whether the battery is factory-fitted (“SAAB BATTERY”) or a replacement battery from another manufacturer (“NON-SAAB”).


Confirm with “SELECT TEST BY SAE(A)” if the battery’s cold starting current is specified according to CCA (SAE) standard. For batteries specified according to DIN standard, select and confirm with “SELECT TEST BY DIN (A)”. ⚠️ Important CCA (SAE) is always applicable for Saab’s factory-fitted batteries The DIN standard can be selected when the analyser is used to test replacement batteries that are not specified according to SAE.


Enter the cold starting current for the battery in question. For Saab factory-fitted batteries, this text is found in capital letters on a label affixed to the top of the battery. After selecting and confirming a value, the actual battery test will start automatically. “SELECT MODE BEFORE CHARGE” “SELECT MODE AFTER CHARGE” Under certain voltage and conductance conditions, the analyser will require information on whether the test is being performed before or after the battery has been charged in order to assess it correctly.


If the analyser indicates the battery needs to be replaced within the warranty period, note the test code. This test code should be included on the warranty claim (more information is available under Warranty policy). ⚠️ Important Also check the replacement battery with the battery analyser before fitting it in the car. If the cold start current of the replacement battery is not specified in accordance with the SAE standard then measurement in accordance with the DIN standard can be selected.


Fit fuses 30 and 37.


Fit the cover of the Underhood Electrical Centre (UEC).


Fit the battery cover.


Carry out Procedure after battery disconnection .

Charging the battery

🔧 Online öffnen

Charging the battery
⚠️ Important
| An auxiliary starting system must not be used as this could damage the electronics of the car.
| To start the car when the battery is discharged, use a booster battery or another car and jumper cables.
|


The battery can normally be charged with a conventional battery charger. Connect the red cable clip to the positive terminal (+) and the black cable clip to chassis ground.


When boost-charging, the battery’s negative terminal must be disconnected. The charging current should not exceed 40 A when boost-charging. Max. charging time: 1.5 hours. ⚠️ Important Never boost-charge a battery if the voltage is below 12 V and the battery is more than 2 years old.


If the battery is completely discharged due to the lights or some other source of consumption having been left on, a weak starting charge should be provided to initiate the chemical process in the battery. If this is the case, start charging with 3 A current (it must not exceed 5 A) for 24 hours or until the charging current has dropped to its lowest stable value. Gas starts to form in the battery at 14.4 V.
If possible, a battery charger capable of delivering a pulsating charging current should be used.

Symptom: Key cannot be turned from LOCK to OFF
/images/9-3-9440/img-im/img5680.svg
Fault symptom
Key cannot be turned from LOCK to OFF
Conditions
No DTCs stored with the fault symptom in question.
Battery voltage greater than 11 V.
Diagnostic help
This symptom can arise if system voltage is low.
⚠️ IMPORTANT
| • | If DTCs are cleared before the fault is remedied, important information on the cause of the fault may be lost and the system may not be able to detect the cause of the fault again. | When DTCs are read out, the diagnostic instrument shows what is blocking the turn of the key.
Most functions that can make it impossible to turn the key are monitored by self-diagnostics and therefore generate DTCs if they are faulty.
Fault diagnosis is only used for faults that are not monitored by self-diagnostics.

5 Speed — Adjustment/replacement Procedures
Gearbox assembly B207

🔧 Online öffnen

Gearbox assembly B207
To remove


Place covers over the wings to keep the paintwork clean and protect it from damage.


Remove the upper engine cover.


Remove the battery cover.


Disconnect the battery terminals and remove the battery and cooling pipe. Undo the cable clamp under the battery tray.


Disconnect the bonnet switch.


Remove the battery tray.


Disconnect the ground cable from the engine bracket and the reversing light switch connection.


Remove the gear cables from the gearbox by pulling the locking sleeves back.


Lift up the cables from the levers.


Fit 30 07 739 Hose pinch-off pliers to the clutch hose and undo the quick-release coupling from the clutch slave cylinder.


Remove the upper bolts from the gearbox.


Unhook the coolant reservoir.


Fit 83 96 178 Lifting eyes, B207 to the engine and 83 94 850 Lifting beam and 83 95 287 Holder . Swap the position of the lifting hooks on the holder.


Relieve the load on the engine and gearbox.


Undo the upper bumper shell mountings.


Suspend two 83 95 212 Strap in place above the radiator core so they are accessible from below.


Raise the car.


Remove the front wheels.


Remove the front spoiler shield. Unplug and remove the connector. CV: Remove Chassis reinforcement, front subframe, CV, petrol


Secure the radiator core with the straps.


Remove the radiator brackets from the subframe.


Remove the exhaust system assembly. ⚠️ Important The flexible bellow on the front section of the exhaust system must not be bent more than 5° from its neutral line. This means that if the front exhaust system is left hanging freely, it must not be bent more than by its own weight. If the strain on the pipe is too great, its component parts will be permanently deformed. This can cause noise, leaks and eventually complete breakdown.


Remove the engine torque rod from the subframe.


Remove the bolt and nut holding the suspension arm to the steering swivel member on both sides.


Unplug the connector and detach the cable clip of the headlamp angle sensor (option)


Remove the steering gear from the subframe.


Put the nuts and washers in a safe place. Let the steering gear hand in place.


Remove the clamps holding the power steering pipe from the subframe.


Detach the front part of the wing liner and bend it slightly out of the way.


Place 83 95 311 Trolley lift , 83 94 801 Parent fixture , 83 95 188 Basic fixture , 83 95 170 Adapter (4 pcs) and 83 96 137 Centring tool, subframe - body under the vehicle. Position the locating pins and adjust the height of the adapters for even pressure.


Remove the subframe bolts and the rear brackets.


Lower the subframe slightly.


Remove the anti-roll bar from the subframe. Protect the steering gear boot.


Pull out the steering arm ball joints from the steering swivel members.


Lower the subframe.


Remove the two torque rod brackets from the gearbox.


Place a receptacle under the car, remove the drain plug. Drain the gearbox oil. Refit the drain plug. Tightening torque 50 Nm (37 lbf ft)


Remove the bolts in the charge air pipe bracket and move away the pipe.


Remove the lower gearbox bolts. Leave one bolt in place.


Detach the ABS cable from the clip using a screwdriver and undo the left-hand drive shaft using 87 92 616 Removal tool, drive shafts .


Suspend the shaft with a 83 95 212 Strap .


Lower the car, mark the positions of the bolts on the left-hand engine bracket with a marker pen for correct refitting and then remove the bolts from the mounting.


Lower the drive unit approx. 70 mm from the lifting beam to facilitate the removal of the gearbox. Measure the distance at the left-hand engine mounting.


Raise the car.


Fit 87 92 608 Holder for single-column lift on a column jack. Adjust and fasten the tool in the gearbox as illustrated.


Remove the last bolt, pull out the transmission and lower it. ⚠️ Important The jack can tip over. Be careful.


Lift the transmission down from the column jack with an engine lift and 87 92 442 Lifting cable while undoing the lifting tool from the transmission.


Plug the holes for the drive shafts with 87 92 665 Protective plug, drive shaft hole if the gearbox is to be transported any distance.


To fit


If necessary, bleed the slave cylinder.


Lubricate the primary shaft splines, see List of lubricants and sealants .


Lubricate the guide sleeves on the engine with anti-corrosion agent.


Fit 83 95 162 Protective collar, drive shafts in the right shaft seal in the transmission. This is done to protect the seal while the transmission is being fitted. Lubricate the seal. ⚠️ Important Always replace the shaft seals in the gearbox. Lubricate with gearbox oil.


Fit the gearbox with the lifting tool on the column jack. ⚠️ Important Make sure the gear cables are positioned correctly when lifting the gearbox. ⚠️ Important Slide in the gearbox until approx. 20 mm are remaining and remove the tool 83 95 162.


Push in the rest of the gearbox. Turn the crankshaft if necessary to get the gearbox in place.


Tighten all bolts except the top one between the engine and the gearbox. Tightening torque, M10 bolts 40 Nm (30 lbf ft) **Tightening torque, M12 bolts 70 Nm (52 lbf ft)


Fit the charge air pipe bracket.


Remove the lifting tool from the gearbox and move away the jack.


Lower the car. Lift in place the power train with the lifting beam until it meets the engine mounting.


Fit the bracket for the engine mounting according to the marks made earlier. Tightening torque 70 Nm +45° (52 lbf ft +45°)


Remove the holder, lifting beam and lifting eyes.


Fit the coolant reservoir.


Fit the upper bolts to the gearbox. Tightening torque 70 Nm (52 lbf ft)


Raise the car.


Fit 83 95 162 Protective collar, drive shafts in the left drive shaft seal. Remove the strap. Make sure that the drive shaft is clean, lubricate it and then align it with the tool. ⚠️ Important Fit the driver in the gearbox until approx.20 mm are remaining and pull out the tool before the sealing surface of the shaft reaches the shaft seal.


Push in the rest of the drive shaft into the gearbox until the circlip clicks in.


Attach the ABS cable to the clip.


Fill with gearbox oil through the level plug hole. See Filling gearbox oil . **Tightening torque: 50 Nm (33 lbf ft)


Fit the two torque rod brackets. Tightening torque 80 Nm (59 lbf ft)


Position the subframe with the help of the fixture. Raise until it is possible to fit the anti-roll bar to the subframe.


Fit the anti-roll bar to the subframe. Tightening torque 18 Nm (13 lbf ft)


Fit the suspension arm ball joints to the steering swivel member. Tightening torque 50 Nm (37 lbf ft) ⚠️ Important Ensure that the steering knuckle stub is visible on the top of the steering knuckle housing before the bolt is fitted.


Check that the guide pins fit into the reference holes, adjust the subframe until the guide pins go in easily and fit the subframe bolts and brackets. Tightening torque, subframe: 75 Nm +135° (55 lbf ft +135°) **Tightening torque, rear subframe bolts: 90 Nm +45° (66 lbf ft +45°)


Connect the connector and the cable clip to the headlamp angle sensor (optional).


Move away the trolley lift and jig.


Fit the torque rods to the subframe. Tightening torque, front: 60 Nm +90° (44 lbf ft +90°) **Tightening torque, rear 80 Nm (59 lbf ft)


Set up 83 96 145 Centring tool kit, subframe - engine and check that the engine is located correctly in relation to the subframe. Remove the centring tool.


Fit the radiator brackets to the subframe. Remove the straps. Tightening torque 47 Nm (35 lbf ft)


Fit the clamps holding the power steering pipe to the subframe.


Fit the steering gear to the subframe. Tightening torque 50 Nm + 60° (37 lbf ft + 60°)


Fit the exhaust system. Tightening torque: 25 Nm (18 lbf ft) ⚠️ Important The flexible bellow on the front section of the exhaust system must not be bent more than 5° from its neutral line. This means that if the front exhaust system is left hanging freely, it must not be bent more than by its own weight. If the strain on the pipe is too great, its component parts will be permanently deformed. This can cause noise, leaks and eventually complete breakdown.


Fit the front wing liner section.


Fit the connector. Fit the front spoiler shield. CV: Fit Chassis reinforcement, front subframe, CV, petrol .


Fit the front wheels.


Lower the car and fit the bumper shell upper mountings.


Check that the upper radiator guides engage their brackets.


Fit the quick-release coupling to the clutch slave cylinder. Remove the hose pinch-off pliers. Make sure the connection is secured in the correct position.


Bleed the clutch. See Bleeding the clutch hydraulic system in the car .


Attach the gear cables to the gearbox.


Check the gear positions and adjust if necessary as described in Adjusting gear cables .


Fit the reversing light switch connection and the ground cable to the engine mounting. Tightening torque 18 Nm (13 lbf ft)


Fit the battery tray and the bonnet switch connector.


Fit the cooling pipe and the battery.


Fit the battery cover.


Fit the upper engine cover.


Remove the wing covers.


Carry out Measures after disconnecting the battery .


Test drive the car. Check the position of the steering wheel when driving straight ahead on a level road. Adjust if needed.


O-ring and sealing ring in seal retainer, left-hand

🔧 Online öffnen

O-ring and sealing ring in seal retainer, left-hand
To remove
[/images/9-3-9440/img-e4/e410r053.svg](saabwisonline.com/images/9-3-9440/img-e4/e410r053.svg)

With gearbox or left drive shaft removed.


Undo the five screws on the seal retainer and remove the seal retainer. Keep shims, screws and the seal retainer in a safe place.


Press out the sealing ring with 87 91 311 Sleeve, driver shaft bearing and 87 92 236 Support, for fitting F35 speed gear .


Detach the O-ring with a small screwdriver or similar.


To fit


Press on the sealing ring to the bottom with 87 92 657 Fitting drift, drive shaft seals . Use 87 92 236 Support, for fitting F35 speed gear for support.


Lubricate a new O-ring and carefully fit it.


Fit the seal retainer and shims with the screws. Tighten alternately. Tightening torque 22 Nm (16 lbf ft)


To dismantle > 🔧 Online öffnen  To dismantle
The gearbox must be cleaned before dismantling.

⚠️ Important
| Holes for drive shafts and delivery line to the slave cylinder must be covered before cleaning the gearbox, use plugs for drive shaft holes 587 92 665.
|
After cleaning the outside of the gearbox, start work as follows


Mount the gearbox on a service stand with 87 92 228 Holder, transmission .


Detach the delivery line. Compress the sleeve on the inside using pliers and push the delivery line forward. Prise up the catch on the sleeve and press in the delivery pipe to detach it.


Undo the slave cylinder screws and remove it.


Remove the bolts for the reverse gear. Note the O-ring!


Remove the end plate. Mark where the ground screw is fitted. Remove the gasket.


Engage 1st gear to lock the gearbox. Refer to the shift arm positions in the illustration. Tap out the retention pin from the 5th gear selector fork. ⚠️ Important Before removing the synchromesh sleeve, mark its position relative to the 5th gear synchromesh with a pen to facilitate refitting. Remove the fork and sleeve and then refit the sleeve.


Press down on the sleeve to engage 5th gear. Two gears must be engaged simultaneously while removing the nut on the output shaft. It is essential that the sleeve is mounted on the synchromesh hub so that the 6 large gear teeth on the sleeve mesh with the 6 deep tooth gaps on the hub.


Knock away the nut lock with a drift on the nut for the output shaft. Remove the nut. ⚠️ Important In all work which involves dismantling the gearbox, a new nut and a new clamping sleeve should be fitted on assembly as the old clamping sleeve will have lost its tension.


Remove the circlip for the 5th gear synchromesh hub. Carefully tap down the hub to make it easier. Lift off the sleeve and then use 87 91 287 Puller, 150 mm , 87 91 303 Arm, 150 mm and 87 92 640 Tool, 5 to lift the 5th gear synchromesh hub (use grease on the tip of the puller). Keep the leaf springs. Then lift up the pinion, baulk ring and needle bearing.


Remove the 5th gear wheel with 87 92 566 Puller, 5 , 89 96 084 Puller, wheel hub and 87 91 410 Sleeve .


Undo the bolts on the differential bearing support.


Remove the bearing support and retain the shims.


Remove the gear selector bracket.


Undo the screw for the reverse shaft support in the gearcase.


Undo and remove the bolts from the mating surface between the gearcase and the clutch housing. Tap down the 2 locating sleeves.


Engage neutral gear.


Fit two 87 92 129 Attachment eye, puller (x 2) . Fit 87 91 410 Sleeve to the output shaft journal. Hook 87 91 287 Puller, 150 mm with 87 91 303 Arm, 150 mm to the eyes and carefully pull off the housing until the pinion and bearing come loose from the shaft. Carefully tap loose the mating surface.


Remove the tools. Lift away the gearcase. ⚠️ Note Put the preload washer on the selector shaft in a safe place.


Tap out the differential bearing race. Use 87 92 202 Sleeve and 87 91 204 Sleeve, bearing race .


Remove the reverse shaft and gear selector fork.


Remove the reverse lever.

Vibrations in gear lever

🔧 Online öffnen

Vibrations in gear lever
Fault symptom
Vibrations and rattling in gear lever.


**Conditions**


Vibration can arise when the driver accelerates in 3rd gear at low speed.


This is due to vibration caused by the engine firing order being conveyed to the gear lever via the gear cables.


**Action**


Proceed as follows in case of customer complaints:



Measure the distance between the gear selector counterbalance and the plastic washer on the gear selector lever housing. Use a feeler gauge and support the counterbalance when measuring, see illustration.


Select the correct number of plastic washers (part no. 904 909 13) according to the table below: Measure the distance (mm) no. of washers 0-0.7 1 0.7 - 1.7 2 1.7 - 2.7 3 2.7 - 3.7 4


To save removing the counterbalance, cut an opening in the washers, 12 mm on the outside diameter and 8 mm on the inside diameter. Support the counterbalance and press the washer onto the rod.

Engage neutral gear.

Move the gear lever to the left. ⚠️ Important Use one finger only to carefully move the lever to the left. Repeat the procedure on the other cable adjuster.


Lift up the adjusting sleeve to its normal position and make sure the catches lock.


Remove the lock pin.


Check the shifting positions.

Replacing gear lever knob > 🔧 Online öffnen  Replacing gear lever knob
To remove


Cover the ignition switch and the area surrounding the gear lever with a cloth or the like.


Use a screwdriver to remove the emblem. ⚠️ Note The emblem varies for rubber or leather knobs.


Cut away the rubber protector in the centre.


Mark and drill a 4 mm hole 5 mm deep into the knob, 3 mm from the edge as illustrated. ⚠️ Warning Wear protective glasses.


Pull of the knob by screwing in a self-threading plate screw with flat tip (25 x 5.5 mm) into the hole.


To fit


Apply glue on the knob as illustrated. Use Thread locking adhesive, Loctite 270 .


Fit the knob to the gear lever. Make sure the spring and foam ring are correctly situated.


Fit the emblem on the gear lever knob. Do not operate the lever until the adhesive has dried (approx. 30 min).


Remove the covering and vacuum up any swarf or the like.

🔧 Online öffnen

Gear cable
To remove


Engage a suitable gear position: 5-speed: position 4. F17 and 6-speed: neutral


Lift the cable connections from the selector arms on the gearbox.


Detach the cables from the cable retainers on the gearbox by pulling back the locking sleeves.


Undo the rubber seal in the bulkhead wall and then the plastic grommet.


Remove the centre console left-hand front side panel.


Remove the gaiter for the air duct.


Undo the plastic cover for the gear lever and the rubber mat in the storage compartment and fold up. Use 82 93 474 Removal tool


Detach the cable adjusters in the gear lever housing with a screwdriver. ⚠️ Important Ensure that the wire adjustment is not damaged.


Press the catches and detach the cable sheaths from the gear lever housing. Lift the air duct slightly with a large screwdriver when the detaching the cable sheaths.


Carefully press a screwdriver blade onto the cable adjuster and pry slightly towards the gear lever. An audible click means that the adjustment catch has been released. Repeat the procedure on the other side of the cable adjuster.


Pull out the cables through the engine bay.


To fit


Insert the cable through the engine bay.


Attach the cable sheaths and cables to the gear lever housing. Fit the black and white cables on the black and white adjusters respectively.


Fit the plastic grommet into the bulkhead wall and the rubber seal.


Fit the cables to the cable retainers on the gearbox by pulling back the locking sleeves. (White to lower retainer and black to upper one)


Attach the cable connections to the selector arms.


Adjust the gear change. See 6-speed: Gear cable adjustment.


Fit the plastic cover for the gear lever and the rubber mat in the storage compartment.


Fit the gaiter for the air duct.


Fit the centre console left-hand front side panel.


Check the shifting positions.

Fine-tune the position of the power train using the adjuster screws. The left and right engine brackets should make the same amount of contact with each engine pad. ⚠️ Important Engine mountings should not lie against the engine brackets.


Tighten the bolts to the prescribed torque.

To fit


Position the driven plate and the pressure plate on the flywheel and loosely tighten the bolts. Vehicles with dual mass flywheel: The convex side of the driven plate should face the gearbox. ⚠️ Important Cars with self-adjusting pressure plate: Clutch plate and pressure plate are matched in pairs and must therefore be replaced as a pair.


Centre the driven plate with B207: 87 92 327 Centring mandrel, clutch plates , man. 6 speed: 83 96 277 Centring mandrel, or Z18XE: 87 92 947 Centring mandrel, clutch plates and tighten the bolts in sequence. Apply 74 96 268 Threadlock to the threads. Tightening torque 30 Nm (22 lbf ft) **Tightening torque, Z18XE/F17 15 Nm (11 lbf ft)

Bleeding the slave cylinder

🔧 Online öffnen

Bleeding the slave cylinder
Removed gearbox is assumed. If gearbox is in-car, see
Bleeding the clutch hydraulic system in the car
.


Connect a 450 mm long piece of clean, transparent 8 mm plastic hose to the slave cylinder delivery pipe connection.


Fully depress the release bearing once and then release it. The slave cylinder seal remains in its inner position.


Fill the plastic hose with brake fluid to a level of about 350 mm.


Connect 30 14 883 Pressure/vacuum pump to the plastic hose. Use a 6 mm plastic hose (this is used to provide a tight seal).


Pump up pressure until the slave cylinder seal moves out and brake fluid runs down into the slave cylinder. The pressure increases when the seal has reached its farthest point.


Remove the pressure/vacuum pump and carefully press in the release bearing to its stop. Note the air bubbles in the plastic hose.


Repeat points 5 to 6 a few times until no air bubbles are visible in the hose.


Leave the slave cylinder seal in its innermost position. Drain and remove the plastic hose.


Bleeding the clutch hydraulic system in the car

🔧 Online öffnen

Bleeding the clutch hydraulic system in the car
For bleeding the slave cylinder, refer to
Bleeding the slave cylinder
.


Unscrew the cover from the brake fluid reservoir.


Top up the brake fluid in the reservoir as necessary.


Undo the bleed nipple.


Connect 88 19 096 Bleeding equipment to the bleed nipple.


Connect compressed air to the bleeding tool and bleed the clutch until clear fluid runs from the nipple.


Tighten the bleed nipple and remove the bleeding tool.


Fit 30 05 451 Adapter, cooling system tester to the brake fluid reservoir.


Press the hose on the brake bleeder against the nipple and bleed the reservoir for about 1 minute, or until no bubbles rise to the surface.


Check clutch operation and top up brake fluid to the correct level.


Refit all components.

If the fluid level is too low to allow for testing in the reservoir, use the pipette and measuring glass.

Brake pads, front, levels 1, 2 and 4
To remove


Raise the car.


Remove the wheel.


Remove the retaining spring from the brake caliper.


Press in the piston by prising with a screwdriver against the brake pad.


Remove the protective covers and guide pins. Lift off the hydraulic body. ⚠️ Note Be careful when handling the brake hose.


Remove the inner brake pad from the caliper and the outer brake pad from the bracket. Clean the inside of the brake caliper and check the dust covers.


To fit


Lubricate the pad sliding surfaces with Special paste .


Place the outer brake pad into the carrier. Fit the inner brake pad into the hydraulic body. ⚠️ Note The inner brake pad must be fitted so that the arrow points in the direction of rotation of the brake disc for forward travel.


Place the hydraulic body into the carrier. Fit the guide pins. Tightening torque 28 Nm (21 lbf ft)


Fit the protective covers.


Fit the retaining spring to the brake caliper. Lay the outer contact surfaces against the bracket and push the centre of the clip.


Fit the wheel .


Lower the car.


Depress the brake pedal repeatedly in order to press out the brake pistons.


Check the brake fluid level and top up as necessary.


Check the operation of the foot brake.

Start by control measuring on one side.


Press in the piston

Control measuring axial hub runout, front wheels


Raise the car and remove the front wheels.


Begin by performing a control measurement on one side.


Press in the piston by prising with a screwdriver against the brake pads.


Remove the brake caliper retaining bolts and lift off the caliper. ⚠️ Note Inspect the wheel sensor cable for damage.


Suspend the caliper with straps.


Remove the brake disc locking bolt.


Lift off the brake disc.

Rotate the hub and check the runout (the value between the highest and lowest reading). If the runout exceeds 0.03 mm, replace the hub. ⚠️ Note The dial gauge should read 0.03-0.05 mm at each bolt hole. This is completely normal.


Remove the dial gauge and bracket.


If the measured runout values are outside the tolerances, replace the hub, see Wheel hub, front .


Clean the contact surfaces between the hub and the brake disc.


Place the brake disc on the hub and fit the brake disc locking bolt. Tightening torque 7 Nm (5 lbf ft)

Fit the wheel .

Lower the car and press the brake pedal in order to press out the brake pads.

Checking brake fluid

🔧 Online öffnen

Checking brake fluid


Test the quality of the brake fluid with 89 96 985 Brake fluid tester . ⚠️ Note It is important that the tester is below the surface of the fluid. LHD: It may be difficult to insert the probe into the reservoir. ⚠️ Warning Never top up with brake fluid before measuring or the measurement will apply to the new brake fluid and give the wrong quality indication. If the fluid level is too low to allow for testing in the reservoir, use the pipette and measuring glass. If the boiling point is below 190°C, change the brake fluid . ⚠️ Note The lowest permissible boiling point for DOT 4 fluid is 155°C. In order that the boiling point should not fall below this level before the next scheduled service, change the fluid if the boiling point falls below 190°C.


Check the fluid level using the MIN and MAX markings on the reservoir. Investigate the cause of low fluid levels. (not during delivery service) Fill with brake fluid if necessary. ⚠️ Note Never use brake fluid from an open container.

Check the function of the steering column lock. ⚠️ Note When the unit has been disconnected from the voltage supply the car must be driven at a speed of at least 7km/h and then stopped before the function is operative.


Fit the sound insulating baffle on the driver’s side .


Steering wheel

🔧 Online öffnen

Steering wheel
To remove


Remove the airbag from the steering wheel.


Turn the steering wheel and wheels to the straight ahead position.


Remove the centre bolt from the steering wheel and lift off the steering wheel.


To fit


Fit the steering wheel onto the steering shaft. ⚠️ Note Make sure the steering wheel fits the key on the steering shaft.


Apply 74 96 268 Thread locking adhesive and fit the centre bolt. Tightening torque 50 Nm (37 lbf ft)


Fit the airbag .


Adjustment handle, steering wheel

🔧 Online öffnen

Adjustment handle, steering wheel
To remove

Press in the catch (A) on the handle and remove the handle.

To fit

Fit the handle to the adjusting arm by pressing until the catch (A) locks.

Column Integration Module, CIM (703)

🔧 Online öffnen

Column Integration Module, CIM (703)
Applies only to the SE, GB and DE markets: Before replacing the control module, carry out regular fault tracing as per WIS and go through
Checklist prior to CIM replacement
.
To remove


Carry out “Procedure before removing the control module” . Remove the steering wheel .


Remove the gaiter from the control module and press it against the instrument panel.


Remove the control module from the steering shaft. Press in the steering column while pulling the control module outwards. ⚠️ Important ⚠️ Take care when releasing the locking mechanism on the connector so as not to damage the connector. Pull the halves straight apart to avoid bending the pins. For further information regarding connectors, refer to Connectors, handling and inspection .


Unplug the connector and remove the clip.


To fit
⚠️ Important
| Take care when plugging in the connector so as not to damage or press out the pins/sleeves in the connector. For further information regarding connectors, refer to
Connectors, handling and inspection
.
|


Plug in the control module connector and fit the clip.


Fit the control module to the steering shaft.


Fit the gaiter to the control module.


Fit the steering wheel .


Carry out “Procedure after changing the control module” .


Suspension arm

🔧 Online öffnen

Suspension arm
To remove


Raise the car.


Remove the front wheel.


Remove the bolt holding the suspension arm to the steering swivel member. Left-hand suspension arm and cars with xenon lights: Remove the level sensor.


Disassemble the suspension arm front attachment to the subframe.


Slacken the bolt which holds the rear bush to the suspension arm.


Remove the rear bush from the subframe.


Remove the suspension arm from the steering swivel member and lift away the suspension arm.


To fit


Lift up the suspension arm and fit the bolt for the front bush.


Fit the rear bush to the subframe. Tightening torque 65 Nm +90° (48 lbf ft +90°)


Fit the suspension arm to the steering swivel member with a new nut. Hold the bolt with a wrench so that the bolt does not rotate. ⚠️ Warning Press up the pin carefully. The groove in the pin must be visible in the screw hole in the spindle housing. If the rubber gaiter is pressed down, it will not seal properly to the swivel pin. Tightening torque 50 Nm (37 lbf ft)


Remove the anti-roll bar link from the anti-roll bar and lift the suspension arm up to normal position.


Tighten the front suspension arm attachment. Tightening torque 65 Nm +90° (48 lbf ft +90°)


Tighten the bolt holding the rear bush to the suspension arm. Tightening torque 40 Nm +30° (30 lbf ft +30°)


Fit the anti-roll bar link. Tightening torque 64 Nm (47 lbf ft) Left-hand suspension arm and cars with xenon lights: Fit the level sensor.


Fit the wheel .


Lower the car to the floor.


Carry out four wheel checking and alignment, see Four wheel alignment .


Track rod, inner

🔧 Online öffnen

Track rod, inner
To remove


Remove the front wheel. 5 x Unscrew bolt


Remove the track rod end. see Track rod, outer .


Remove the rubber gaiter. see Gaiter, steering gear . ⚠️ Important: Grip the steering gear rack when removing/tightening the track rod thrust joint, in order to avoid damaging the rack. Wrench surface for counterstay on the rack is only on the gear side. For this reason, when removing/fitting the opposite track rod, both rubber gaiters must be removed from the steering gear.


Remove the track rod (1). Unscrew using KM-6321 ( 89 97 009 Special wrench for EHPS, 89 96 837 Special wrench for others) (2) - Grip the rack by the flats (arrow) with an open wrench (3). To fit


Important: Grip the steering gear rack when removing/tightening the track rod thrust joint, in order to avoid damaging the rack. Wrench surface for counterstay on the rack is only on the gear side. For this reason, when removing/fitting the opposite track rod, both rubber gaiters must be removed from the steering gear. Fit the track rod (1). Tighten using KM-6321 ( 89 97 009 Special wrench for EHPS, 89 96 837 Special wrench for others) (2) (90 Nm) - Grip the rack by the flats (arrow) with an open wrench (3).


Fit the rubber gaiter and outer track rod. see Gaiter, steering gear .


Fit the front wheel . Checking/inspection


Check wheel angles and adjust as necessary. See Wheel alignment .


Track rod end

🔧 Online öffnen

Track rod end
To remove


Raise the car.


Remove the wheel.


Slacken the lock nut.


Remove the nut securing the track rod end to the steering swivel member.


Part the track rod end from the steering swivel member with 87 91 287 Puller, 150 mm.


Unscrew the track rod end from the track rod, counting the number of turns.


To fit


Screw on the track rod end the same number of turns as when it was removed. ⚠️ Note The left and right track-rod ends are different. The track rod ends should curve slightly backwards when fitted. Markings: L = left-hand side, R = right-hand side.


Bolt the track rod end to the steering swivel member. Tightening torque 35 Nm (26 lbf ft)


Tighten the track rod end’s locknut. Tightening torque 70 Nm (52 lbf ft)


Fit the wheel . Tightening torque 110 Nm (81 lbf ft) Lower the car to the floor.


Check the toe-in angle using 88 19 013 Gauge, toe-in and adjust the toe-in angle as necessary.


Calibrate the steering wheel angle sensor .


Gaiter, steering gear

🔧 Online öffnen

Gaiter, steering gear
To remove


Raise the car.


Remove the wheel.


Slacken the locknut.


Remove the nut securing the track rod end to the steering swivel member.


Part the track rod end from the steering swivel member with 87 91 287 Puller, 150 mm .


Unscrew the track rod end from the track rod, counting the number of turns.


Blow the area clean with compressed air and remove the clips from the gaiter. Pull off the gaiter.


To fit


If necessary, carefully wipe the track rod clean and examine the ball joint. ⚠️ Important If sand, gravel or other contaminants enter the ball joint (e.g. if the boot has been defective for a time), the track rod must be changed.


Fit a new gaiter to the track rod and steering gear housing. Fit new clips using 30 16 235 Pliers to secure them.


Screw on the track rod end the same number of turns as when it was removed. ⚠️ Note The left and right track-rod ends are different. The track rod ends should curve slightly backwards when fitted. Markings: L = left-hand side, R = right-hand side.


Bolt the track rod end to the steering swivel member. Tightening torque 35 Nm (26 lbf ft)


Tighten the track rod end’s locknut. Tightening torque 70 Nm (55 lbf ft)


Fit the wheel .


Lower the car to the floor.


Check the toe-in and adjust if required. For setting values, refer to Wheel geometry .


Steering swivel member

🔧 Online öffnen

Steering swivel member
To remove


Remove the wheel hub .


Remove the track rod end from the steering swivel member.


Remove the steering swivel member from the MacPherson strut. Hold the bolt with a wrench so that the bolt does not rotate.


To fit


Fit the steering swivel member to the MacPherson strut. Hold the bolt with a wrench so that the bolt does not rotate. Tightening torque 80 Nm +135° (59 lbf ft +135°)


Fit the track rod end to the steering swivel member. Tightening torque 35 Nm (26 lbf ft)


Fit the wheel hub .


Four wheel alignment

🔧 Online öffnen

Four wheel alignment
Use the equipment for four wheel checking.
The rear wheels must be adjusted before the front wheels. For further information, see
[Technical description Wheel geometry](saabwisonline.com/9-3-9440/2005/7-suspension-wheels/front-suspension/technical-description/wheel-geometry)
and
[Technical data Wheel geometry](saabwisonline.com/9-3-9440/2005/7-suspension-wheels/front-suspension/technical-data/wheel-geometry)
.

Rear wheels
When setting rear wheel geometry, camber will be affected by toe-in adjustment and vice versa. It is important to follow the instructions carefully during alignment.


[/images/9-3-9440/img-f6/f631r030.svg](saabwisonline.com/images/9-3-9440/img-f6/f631r030.svg)

| A. | Adjust toe-in by rotating the off-centre screw located in the toe-in link mounting in the subframe. | | B. | Adjust camber by rotating the off-centre screw located in the lower suspension arm mounting in the subframe. | When adjusting rear wheel geometry, remove approximately half of the total error from the side with the most incorrect angle. Then adjust the other angle by approximately half the total error.
Adjust the first angle error by half and so on until both settings are correct.
Tightening torque 75 Nm +60° (55 lbf ft +60°) Hold the bolt and tighten the nut.**
Front wheels
/images/9-3-9440/img-f6/f631r031.svg
| • | Toe-in is adjusted by lengthening or shortening the track rods.
Toe-in must be adjusted by an equal amount on both left-hand and right-hand track rods to ensure that the steering wheel spokes will be positioned symmetrically. | Tightening torque 70 Nm (52 lbf ft)
⚠️ Note
| Calibration of steering angle sensor
must be carried out after realigning the wheels on cars with ESP.
Wheel hub, front

🔧 Online öffnen

Wheel hub, front
To remove


Raise the car.


Remove the wheel.


Remove the hub nut.


Press in the drive shaft so that it loosens from the hub 89 96 951 Puller, hub drive shaft .


Press in the piston by prising with a screwdriver against the brake pads.


|  | - | Levels 1, 2 and 4
Prise against the brake pad using a screwdriver. |  | - | Level 3:
Prise between the brake disc and brake caliper using a screwdriver. 6. Remove the brake caliper and suspend it from the spring


Remove the brake disc lock bolt and lift off the brake disc.


Remove the wheel sensor connection.


Remove the bolt securing the suspension arm ball joint to the steering swivel member.


Pull out the ball joint pin.


Place a wedge between the suspension arm and the anti-roll bar in order to hold down the suspension arm.


Pull the drive shaft out from the hub and lift the hub and steering swivel member from the shaft. ⚠️ Note ⚠️ Take care that the inner universal joint does not separate.


Remove the three bolts from the hub. Lift off the hub and the brake shield.


To fit


Clean the contact surfaces and fit the brake shield and the hub with three bolts. Make sure that the cable to the wheel sensor fits into position upwards/forwards. Tightening torque 90 Nm +45° (66 lbf ft +45°)


Insert the drive shaft into the hub. ⚠️ Important Always fit a new hub-centre nut if it has been removed because the clamping force of the lock indentations will be reduced if the old one is refitted.


Fit the hub nut and pull the shaft to the correct position with the nut.


Remove the wedge and fit the suspension arm to the steering swivel member. Tightening torque 50 Nm (37 lbf ft) ⚠️ Warning Check that the spindle on the ball joint protrudes above the steering swivel member attachment.


Clean the brake disc surfaces thoroughly. Fit the brake disc into place and tighten the brake disc bolts. Tightening torque 7 Nm (5 lbf ft)


Connect the wheel sensor and fit the connector into the holder.


Fit the brake caliper. Tightening torque 210 Nm +30° (155 lbf ft +30°)


Fit the wheel .


Lower the car so that the wheel rests on the floor.


Tighten the hub nut. Tightening torque 230 Nm (170 lbf ft)


Fit the centre emblem.


Press out the piston in the brake caliper.


Suspension arm bush, front

🔧 Online öffnen

Suspension arm bush, front
To remove


Remove the suspension arm .


Lubricate the bush with soapy water.


Press out the bush using KM-508-1 from Press tools 89 96 787 as well as the pull rod and KM-907-23 from 89 96 779 Press sleeve set, front chassis .


To fit


Lubricate the bush with soapy water.


Press the bush into the suspension arm using KM-907-13 from 89 96 779 Set of press sleeves, front assembly as well as KM-508-3 and KM-508-4 from 89 96 787 Set of press sleeves, front link arms in a hydraulic press.


Fit the suspension arm .


Steering links, checking

🔧 Online öffnen

Steering links, checking
/images/9-3-9440/img-f6/f631r032.svg


Check the wear of the outer ball joints and the inner bearings. They should not have play.


Check the protective gaiters.


Check the threads of the toe-in adjuster. Anti-corrosion agent should be applied if the threads show any sign of corrosion.


Steering Linkage — Fault diagnosis Procedures
Metallic noise from front end/brakes

🔧 Online öffnen

Metallic noise from front end/brakes
Symptom: Metallic noise from front end/brakes. The noise can be misinterpreted as a faulty/damaged wheel bearing.
The noise occurs during slow driving, when turning the steering wheel and, in some cases, when the brakes are applied lightly.
Conditions
15”, 16” or 16"+ brake system.

Fault symptom
Metallic noise from front end/brakes. The noise can be misinterpreted as a faulty/damaged wheel bearing.


The noise occurs during slow driving, when turning the steering wheel and, in some cases, when the brakes are applied lightly.


**Cause:**
The brake anchor plate moves and scrapes against the steering swivel member.

Procedure


Slacken the wheel hub bolts (A).


Carefully use a rubber mallet to tap the top of the brake anchor plate (B) until it is in its bottom position.


Tighten the wheel hub bolts. Tightening torque 90 Nm +45° (66 lbf ft +45°)


Compare List > 🔧 Online öffnen  Symptom:

Diagnostic help
To compare the customer's car with another almost identical car, which you know is in full working order, helps to establish whether the customer's problem can be a characteristic of the car's design. To reach a valid conclusion, the comparison should be performed under the same conditions and with the same criteria on a car that has the same optional equipment as the customer's car.

Front Suspension — Adjustment/replacement Procedures
Subframe, B207

🔧 Online öffnen

Subframe, B207
To remove


Remove the upper bumper shell attachments.


Hang two 83 95 212 Straps in place over the radiator member and the radiator unit so that they are accessible from below.


Raise the car.


Remove the front wheels.


Remove the lower front cover. CV: Remove Chassis reinforcement, front subframe, CV .


Bind the radiator unit tightly with the straps.


Remove the radiator brackets from the subframe.


Remove Exhaust system assembly . ⚠️ Important ⚠️ Take care so as not to crack the flex bellows.


Remove the engine torque rod from the subframe.


Remove the bolt and nut which attach the suspension arm to the steering swivel member on both sides. Left-hand suspension arm and cars with xenon lights: Remove the level sensor.


Remove the steering gear from the subframe. Mind the nuts and washers. Allow the steering gear to remain suspended.


Open the clips that secure the power steering pipe to the subframe.


Remove the front part of the wing liner and fold away slightly.


Position the 83 95 311 Trolley lift underneath with 83 94 801 Parent fixture and 83 96 137 Removal/fitting tool, subframe .


Remove the subframe bolts on both sides. Remove the stays from the body.


Lower the subframe slightly.


Pull out the suspension arms ball-and-socket joints from the steering swivel members.


Remove the anti-roll bar from the subframe.


Lower the subframe.


Subframe replacement: Remove the suspension arms and rear torque rod.


To fit


Place the frame on the 83 95 311 Trolley lift with 83 94 801 Parent fixture and 83 96 137 Removal/fitting tool, subframe .


Subframe replacement: Fit the rear torque rod and the suspension arms in the horizontal position. Rear torque rod: 60 Nm (44 lbf ft) Rear bush to subframe 65 Nm +135° (48 lbf ft +135°) Front bush to subframe 65 Nm +135° (48 lbf ft +135°)


Lift the frame. Fit the ball joints for the suspension arms in the steering swivel member. Fit the anti-roll bar to the subframe. The opening of the rubber bushes should face forward (M05 only)


Lift the subframe into place and align 83 96 137 Centring tool, subframe - body with the locating holes in the body.


Attach the power steering pipe to the plastic clips on the subframe.


Lift the subframe so that the inner sections of the bushes are pressing against the body. Fit the front subframe bolts on both sides. Tightening torque 75 Nm +135° (55 lbf ft +135°)** Fit the stays and the rear subframe bolts on both sides. Enter the rear stay bolts before tightening the subframe bolts. Tightening torque 75 Nm +135° (55 lbf ft +135°)** Lower and pull away the trolley lift.


Tighten the rear stay bolts. Tightening torque 90 Nm +45° (66 lbf ft +45°)


Fit the steering gear with bolts, washers and nuts. Tightening torque 50 Nm +60° (37 lbf ft +60°)


Fit the engine torque rod to the subframe. Tightening torque, rear torque rod 80 Nm (59 lbf ft) Tightening torque, front torque rod 60 Nm +90° (44 lbf ft +90°) Set up 83 96 145 Centring tool, subframe - engine and check that the engine is correctly positioned in relation to the subframe. Remove the centring tool.


Fit the suspension arms to the steering swivel members. ⚠️ Warning Press up the pin carefully. The groove in the pin must be visible in the screw hole in the spindle housing. If the rubber gaiter is pressed down, it will not seal properly to the swivel pin. Tightening torque 50 Nm (37 lbf ft) Left-hand suspension arm and cars with xenon lights: Fit the level sensor.


Fit the radiator brackets to the subframe. ⚠️ Note Check that the upper radiator unit support is placed correctly.


Remove the straps.


Fit Exhaust system assembly . ⚠️ Important ⚠️ Take care so as not to crack the flex bellows.


Fit the front part of the wing liner on both sides of the car.


CV: Fit Chassis reinforcement, front subframe, CV . Fit the lower front cover.


Fit the wheels .


Lower the car to the floor.


Fit the upper bumper shell attachments.


Check the straight-ahead position of the steering wheel when driving on a level road. Adjust if necessary.


Replacement of subframe : Carry out Four wheel alignment .


Subframe bush

🔧 Online öffnen

Subframe bush
⚠️ Note
| This method involves destructive disassembly. It is not possible to refit the old bush.
To remove


Remove the subframe. See Subframe B207 or Subframe, remove and install, Z19 .


Cut away the rubber from the bush.


Saw or cut a groove on either side. Break off the flange from the bush to make room for the support.


Cut away the rubber edge protruding from the underside of the bush.


Remove the bush using a pull rod 907 and press sleeve KM 907-14 from 89 96 779 Set of press sleeves, front assembly and a support from 89 96 902 Subframe bush set


To fit
⚠️ Note
| Make sure the bush is pressed in straight.


Press in the bush using sleeves from the 89 96 902 Subframe bush set .


Fit the subframe. See Subframe B207 or Subframe, remove and install, Z19.


MacPherson strut

🔧 Online öffnen

MacPherson strut
To remove


Raise the car.


Remove the wheel.


Remove the upper nut from the anti-roll bar link, hold with a 17 mm open wrench.


Remove the holder for the wheel sensor connector housing and the brake hose clip.


Relieve the steering spindle member from bearing weight using a jack. Allow the jack to remain during the entire operation.


Remove the steering swivel member from the MacPherson strut. Hold the bolt with a wrench so that the bolt does not rotate.


Withdraw the steering swivel member from the suspension strut.


Remove the bolts from the upper attachment of the MacPherson strut.


Remove the MacPherson strut.


To fit


Position the MacPherson strut into place and fit the bolts in the upper attachment. ⚠️ Note The fitting holes are not symmetrical. Tighten the bolts alternately. Tightening torque 19 Nm (14 lbf ft)


Raise the steering swivel member against the MacPherson strut, press the steering swivel member into the MacPherson strut. Fit the bolts and tighten the nuts holding the steering swivel member to the MacPherson strut. Hold with a wrench so that the bolt does not rotate. Tightening torque 80 Nm +135° (59 lbf ft +135°)


Fit the upper nut to the anti-roll bar link. Tightening torque 64 Nm (47 lbf ft)


Fit the bracket for the wheel sensor cable. Fit the brake hose and clip.


Fit the wheel .


Lower the car to the floor.


MacPherson strut, dismantling and assembling

Fault symptom
Rattling noise from front shock absorber when driving on an uneven surface at speeds below 20 km/h.

Conditions
Rattling noise from front shock absorber when driving on an uneven surface at speeds below 20 km/h. The noise comes from inside the shock absorber when the piston is at dead centre position.

Procedure
Replace both MacPherson struts and the springs, see
[MacPherson strut, dismantling and assembling.](saabwisonline.com/9-3-9440/2005/7-suspension-wheels/front-suspension/adjustment-replacement/macpherson-strut-dismantling-and-assembling)

🔧 Online öffnen

Noise in the MacPherson strut
Background
Certain cars have no water shield fitted and this may allow water to enter the thrust bearing and cause corrosion.

Fault symptom
Knocking noise while turning the steering wheel, or banging noise when driving on uneven roads.

Procedure


Remove the MacPherson strut .


Disassemble the MacPherson strut .


Replace the thrust bearing (B).


Reassemble the MacPherson strut . ⚠️ Important Fit the water shield (A), with the part number upwards, between the thrust bearing (B) and the dust excluder (C).


Fit the MacPherson strut .

Fault symptom
A disruptive noise which is coming from the front assembly.

Conditions
If a bolt connection has settled, noise can occur when the upper and lower nuts on the anti-roll bar link lose tightening torque.
Procedure
Check that the tightening torque is correct. Tighten both nuts.
